method.source_id_policy: No web source IDs fabricated; exact primary URLs recorded.
method.limit: Paid standards full text not read. Catalog scope verifies identity and broad context only. Existing manuscript correctness is assessed at cited-claim scope, not by title alone.

summary.remaining_citation_scope_fix: part11 related-work sentence needs narrowing unless root applies the supplied remedy

entries.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
entries.publication_status: Cited as an arXiv preprint; v1 2025-03-24, v2 2025-06-24. The inspected arXiv page does not assign a journal/conference publication.
entries.cited_claim: CaMeL uses capability-based information-flow control to govern data/tool behavior.
entries.source_summary: CaMeL separates trusted-query control/data flows and applies capabilities/security policies at tool invocation to constrain unauthorized data flows. This directly supports the narrow related-work description; it supplies no evidence of this manuscript's implementation or physical safety.

entries.title: Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures — Scope and Application
entries.publication_status: Final FDA guidance, September 2003; public page content-current date 2018-08-24. Guidance is nonbinding and is distinct from the regulation originally issued in 1997.
entries.read_scope: FDA guidance HTML, including scope, authority checks, electronic signatures, audit trails, and nonbinding-status sections
entries.cited_claim: Original related-work sentence groups range checks, approvals, versioned recipes, and audit trails in DCS/SCADA and electronic batch-record practice under this one citation.
entries.source_summary: The guidance covers defined FDA-regulated electronic records/signatures, authority/operational/device checks, and risk-based audit/record controls. It does not establish generic DCS/SCADA range-check practice or recipe-version control. It expressly discusses narrow applicability and enforcement discretion.
changes: Use exact guidance title without prefixing it as the regulation itself; set howpublished to Guidance for Industry and include official FDA URL.

Narrow the citation-bearing sentence to electronic-record/signature accountability, authority checks, and risk-based audit trails; support range/recipe practices with ISA-88 or implementation evidence separately.
Do not describe this system as Part 11 compliant or certified.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: IEC 62443-3-3:2013: Industrial communication networks — Network and system security — Part 3-3: System security requirements and security levels
entries.publication_status: Published 2013-08-07; catalog stability date 2027; 2014 corrigendum included.
entries.read_scope: Public IEC catalog metadata and scope only; paid standard full text not read
entries.cited_claim: Industrial control-system security environment / deployment credentials, endpoint security, and IT/OT separation.
entries.source_summary: The public scope identifies technical control-system security requirements and capability security levels, applied using zones and conduits. It supports broad IACS security context; individual clauses, implementation compliance, and certification were not assessed.
changes: Retain as security-context reference; avoid asserting formal IEC 62443 compliance or implying catalog access proves every detailed deployment clause.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: IEEE Standard for Electric Power Systems Communications—Distributed Network Protocol (DNP3)
entries.publication_status: IEEE SA catalog: published 2012-10-10; Inactive-Reserved since 2023-03-30. Historical reference, not an active-current-standard claim.
entries.read_scope: IEEE SA public standard catalog; DNP Users Group original 8-page Primer, Revision A, 2005-03-20, p.7
entries.cited_claim: DNP3 select-before-operate is a telecontrol precedent for staged command handling.
entries.source_summary: IEEE's catalog verifies the designation/title and protocol scope. The DNP Users Group primer explicitly describes control and analog-output requests using select-before-operate or direct-operate sequences on page 7. This does not equate command staging with observing physical process attainment.
changes: Add historical wording if needed; do not label IEEE1815-2012 active/current.
No full paid IEEE standard was accessed; SBO claim was checked using the protocol owner's public primer.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding
entries.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
entries.publication_status: Published AAAI-18 conference paper; publisher landing page lists 2018-04-29.
entries.read_scope: AAAI publisher metadata/abstract plus original PDF first page and page-number footers
entries.cited_claim: Formal shielding is a distinct safety-enforcement approach that complements supervisory governance.
entries.source_summary: The work synthesizes a shield from temporal-logic specifications, monitors learner actions, and corrects actions that would violate the specification. Its formal-property setting supports distinguishing shielding from this manuscript's supervisory checks.
changes: Add pages={2669--2678}; the original publisher PDF has 10 pages with these printed page numbers.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Control Barrier Function Based Quadratic Programs for Safety Critical Systems
entries.publication_status: Published in August 2017 issue; online date 2016-12-13 is not a conflicting publication year.
entries.read_scope: IEEE publisher metadata/abstract and introduction; author arXiv abstract/related DOI
entries.cited_claim: Control-barrier-function safety certification differs from ordinary range/admission checks.
entries.source_summary: The paper formalizes forward invariance via barrier functions and combines safety constraints with Lyapunov performance objectives in quadratic programs. It supports the manuscript's methodological distinction; no CBF proof is supplied for this system.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Using simplicity to control complexity
entries.publication_status: Published July–August 2001 issue; IEEE date of publication 2001-08-31.
entries.read_scope: IEEE publisher metadata, article introduction, and The Simplex Architecture section
entries.cited_claim: Simplex assurance is a distinct mechanism with a reliable safety/core controller and switching logic.
entries.source_summary: The Simplex section separates high-assurance and high-performance subsystems and uses decision logic to retain the plant within an established stability envelope or hand control to the assurance controller. It supports differentiation from a software supervisory record/admission layer.
changes: Capitalize Simplex when naming the architecture.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation: An Attentional Integration
entries.publication_status: Published research review; publisher first-online date 2010-10-20.
entries.read_scope: SAGE publisher metadata/abstract; page extent also checked in publisher's rights-link metadata (startPage=381,endPage=410)
entries.cited_claim: Approval workflow structure is distinguishable from measured operator comprehension, complacency, and automation bias.
entries.source_summary: The review integrates evidence on automation-related complacency and bias, highlighting attention, multitask load, and omission/commission errors. It motivates human evaluation, but it does not diagnose this system or show its operators experience those effects.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: A model for types and levels of human interaction with automation
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics—Part A: Systems and Humans
entries.cited_claim: Human responsibility and automation allocation require explicit design beyond adding a confirmation click.
entries.source_summary: The model distinguishes acquisition, analysis, decision/action selection, and action implementation and their levels of automation. Human performance consequences are primary design-evaluation criteria. It supports the workflow-versus-human-outcome distinction.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Ironies of automation
entries.publication_status: Published November 1983; 2021 author-site posting is a reproduction, not the paper's publication year.
entries.read_scope: Elsevier publisher issue/article metadata and abstract; author's reproduced original paper, including monitoring/manual-takeover/human-computer collaboration sections
entries.cited_claim: Automation changes residual operator tasks and responsibility; human collaboration is a separate evaluation concern.
entries.source_summary: The original discusses monitoring and manual takeover, maintenance of manual/cognitive skills, and human-computer collaboration in industrial process control. It supports discussing the human role without asserting a demonstrated defect in this system.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 16th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec '23)
entries.publication_status: Published 2023-11-26; publisher notes corrected version of record on 2024-01-10 with minor nonsubstantive changes, same work/DOI.
entries.read_scope: ACM publisher metadata, editorial note, and author-supplied abstract; arXiv author record/abstract. Publisher AI-generated summary was not used.
entries.cited_claim: Retrieved documents/prompts are treated as untrusted inputs at the execution boundary.
entries.source_summary: The paper demonstrates indirect injection through retrieved data that can redirect application behavior and API invocation. It supports separating retrieved content from authority; it is not evidence of an exploit or a completed attack evaluation in the submitted system.
entries.freshness_note: Older than two years; used as a foundational/historical reference.

entries.title: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
entries.publication_status: Published USENIX Security 2024 proceedings paper; official open-access record.
entries.cited_claim: Prompt injection warrants an explicit untrusted-input boundary and separately measured attack evaluation.
entries.source_summary: The authors formalize prompt injection and evaluate attacks/defenses across multiple models/tasks. The narrow contextual citation is appropriate. It does not establish this system's defense effectiveness or lack of vulnerabilities.
